data.narrative:
Mimic Robotics is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Stefan Weirich, Stephan-Daniel Gravert, Elvis Nava, Benedek Forrai, and Robert Katzschmann. The company has raised $16M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a broader universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable in Robotics & Manufacturing, including companies such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable approach. Using $16M in total raised as a value proxy and applying a standard 2.5x multiplier for progression from seed to the subsequent stage yields an implied valuation of $40M. The peer-median approach was not applied; while 11 same-sector peers exist, the narrow peer set—filtered by stage, adjacency, and valuation tier—does not contain sufficient datapoints (minimum 3 required) to generate a reliable median. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias given the dispersion in robotics company profiles and maturity levels.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $34M to $46M, with a median point of $40M. The range reflects ±15% variance around the stage-progression result to account for execution risk and company-specific factors. Key uncertainties include the absence of a robust peer median and limited public market comparables in this subsector, both of which constrain confidence in the valuation floor and ceiling.
